DECISION. Split dph_sh_affine_estimate into two new, dependency-free children. They are the two current-free obligations of the supplied proof.
(i) Step 1: smoothness of the straight-line homotopy G(y) = F₀(tl y) + t(y)(F₁ − F₀)(tl y) and its slice derivative, dG = (F₁ − F₀)dt + ((1−t)DF₀ + tDF₁)dx.

Both are classical facts about the straight-line homotopy (Simon Ch. 6, 2.25–2.27, 2.29), and both are reused elsewhere. The grandparent's supplied proof needs "G_ij(t,x) = G_i(x) + t(G_j(x) − G_i(x)) is C^∞ and proper on [0,1] × spt X" (Part 5.1) and the same for ĥ_σ (6.11). The accepted iwl_cr_ci_cone_map is the direct precedent: it splits off the analogous calculus fact for the cone map. The two children are independent, so they can be formalized in parallel. Together they are about 100 of the roughly 250 Lean lines of the full proof (measured on the scratch proofs below).
The selected node keeps the current-theoretic assembly: supplied step 2 (closedness of spt X only) and steps 4–10. The runtime waits on and overlays children + depends_on for a parent (runtime.py _overlay_accepted_children and _wait_for_accepted_dependencies; speculation.contract), so these need not be repeated as children. subproblems.title: Straight-line homotopy G = F₀∘tl + t·(F₁ − F₀)∘tl is C^∞, with DG(cons(s,x))e₀ = F₁(x) − F₀(x) and DG(cons(s,x))(ιv) = (1 − s)DF₀(x)v + sDF₁(x)v
subproblems.statement:
Let m, m′ ∈ ℕ and let F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)).

Notation:
- ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p).
- For y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}: t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)).
- For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)).
- ι(v) := cons(0, v) for v ∈ ℝ^m, and e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}.
- D := fderiv ℝ.

Let G : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m′}, G(y) := F₀(tl y) + t(y)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)). This is the straight-line homotopy from F₀ to F₁, written exactly as the map G of dph_sh_affine_estimate.

Then G is C^∞, and for all s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m:
- DG(cons(s, x))(e₀) = F₁(x) − F₀(x);
- DG(cons(s, x))(ι(v)) = (1 − s)·DF₀(x)(v) + s·DF₁(x)(v) for every v ∈ ℝ^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' : ℕ) (F₀ F₁ : Eucl m → Eucl m'), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) F₀ → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) F₁ → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (fun y : Eucl (m + 1) => F₀ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))) + (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y 0) • (F₁ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))) - F₀ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))))) ∧ ∀ (s : ℝ) (x : Eucl m), fderiv ℝ (fun y : Eucl (m + 1) => F₀ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))) + (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y 0) • (F₁ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))) - F₀ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))))) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x))) (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = F₁ x - F₀ x ∧ ∀ v : Eucl m, fderiv ℝ (fun y : Eucl (m + 1) => F₀ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))) + (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y 0) • (F₁ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))) - F₀ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ y))))) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x))) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v))) = (1 - s) • fderiv ℝ F₀ x v + s • fderiv ℝ F₁ x v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of dph_sh_affine_estimate (Simon Ch. 6, 2.27: dh = (F₁ − F₀)dt + ((1 − t)DF₀ + tDF₁)dx for the straight-line homotopy h), with all details filled in. Notation as in the statement. Put e := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ and e′ := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ; both are continuous linear equivalences.

1. (The coordinate maps are continuous linear.) Define tL := (ContinuousLinearMap.proj 0) ∘L e : ℝ^{m+1} →L[ℝ] ℝ and tlL := e′.symm ∘L (ContinuousLinearMap.pi (j ↦ ContinuousLinearMap.proj j.succ)) ∘L e : ℝ^{m+1} →L[ℝ] ℝ^m. Since Fin.tail q = (j ↦ q (j.succ)), we have tL(y) = t(y) and tlL(y) = tl(y) for every y, both by definition (rfl). Hence G(y) = F₀(tlL y) + tL(y)·(F₁(tlL y) − F₀(tlL y)) for all y (rfl).

2. (Values on cons, ι and e₀.) Let τ ∈ ℝ and z ∈ ℝ^m. Then e(cons(τ, z)) = Fin.cons τ (e′ z), so tL(cons(τ, z)) = (Fin.cons τ (e′ z)) 0 = τ (Fin.cons_zero). Also tlL(cons(τ, z)) = e′.symm (Fin.tail (Fin.cons τ (e′ z))) = e′.symm (e′ z) = z (Fin.tail_cons, ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply). Both identities even hold definitionally. With τ = 0 and z = v this gives tL(ι v) = 0 and tlL(ι v) = v. Moreover e(e₀) = Pi.single 0 1 (PiLp.ofLp_single), so tL(e₀) = 1. Since j.succ ≠ 0 for every j : Fin m, we get tlL(e₀) = e′.symm (j ↦ (Pi.single 0 1) j.succ) = e′.symm 0 = 0.

3. (G is C^∞.) Continuous linear maps are C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff). So F₀∘tlL and F₁∘tlL are C^∞ (ContDiff.comp), hence so is their difference F₁∘tlL − F₀∘tlL (ContDiff.sub). The product of the C^∞ real function tL with that difference is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul), and adding F₀∘tlL keeps the map C^∞ (ContDiff.add). By step 1 the result is G, so G is C^∞.

4. (The derivative of G at an arbitrary point.) Since ∞ ≠ 0, F₀ and F₁ are differentiable (ContDiff.differentiable), so HasFDerivAt F_i (DF_i(z)) z for every z and i = 0, 1. Fix y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}.
   - Chain rule with the linear map tlL (HasFDerivAt.comp, ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt): y ↦ F_i(tlL y) has derivative DF_i(tlL y) ∘L tlL at y.
   - Difference rule: y ↦ F₁(tlL y) − F₀(tlL y) has derivative DF₁(tlL y) ∘L tlL − DF₀(tlL y) ∘L tlL.
   - Product rule for the scalar factor tL (HasFDerivAt.smul: D(c·f)(y) = c(y)·Df(y) + (Dc(y)).smulRight(f(y)), where Dc(y) = tL because tL is linear), then the sum rule (HasFDerivAt.add). By HasFDerivAt.fderiv this gives
   DG(y) = DF₀(tlL y) ∘L tlL + tL(y)·(DF₁(tlL y) ∘L tlL − DF₀(tlL y) ∘L tlL) + tL.smulRight(F₁(tlL y) − F₀(tlL y)).
   Evaluated at h ∈ ℝ^{m+1}:
   DG(y)h = DF₀(tl y)(tl h) + t(y)·(DF₁(tl y)(tl h) − DF₀(tl y)(tl h)) + t(h)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)).

5. (The value at e₀.) Let y = cons(s, x). By step 2, tl y = x, t y = s, tl e₀ = 0 and t e₀ = 1. Step 4 then gives DG(y)e₀ = DF₀(x)0 + s·(DF₁(x)0 − DF₀(x)0) + 1·(F₁(x) − F₀(x)) = 0 + s·0 + (F₁(x) − F₀(x)) = F₁(x) − F₀(x). The rules used are map_zero, sub_zero, smul_zero, one_smul and zero_add.

6. (The value at ι v.) Let y = cons(s, x) and v ∈ ℝ^m. By step 2, tl(ι v) = v and t(ι v) = 0, so step 4 gives
   DG(y)(ι v) = DF₀(x)v + s·(DF₁(x)v − DF₀(x)v) + 0·(F₁(x) − F₀(x)) = DF₀(x)v + s·DF₁(x)v − s·DF₀(x)v = (1 − s)·DF₀(x)v + s·DF₁(x)v.
   The rules used are zero_smul, add_zero, smul_sub, sub_smul, one_smul and commutativity of addition.

Step 3 proves the first conjunct, and steps 5 and 6 prove the two derivative identities for all s, x and v. ∎
proof_key_steps: t and tl are continuous linear maps tL = proj 0 ∘L e and tlL = e′.symm ∘L pi(proj ∘ succ) ∘L e, with tL(cons(τ,z)) = τ, tlL(cons(τ,z)) = z, tL(e₀) = 1 and tlL(e₀) = 0; G = F₀∘tlL + tL·(F₁∘tlL − F₀∘tlL) by rfl.
G is C^∞, because C^∞ maps are closed under composition with linear maps, sums, differences and scalar products.
Chain and product rules: DG(y) = DF₀(tl y)∘tlL + t(y)(DF₁(tl y)∘tlL − DF₀(tl y)∘tlL) + tL.smulRight(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)).
At y = cons(s,x): DG(y)e₀ = F₁(x) − F₀(x) and DG(y)(ιv) = DF₀(x)v + s(DF₁(x)v − DF₀(x)v) = (1 − s)DF₀(x)v + sDF₁(x)v.

subproblems.title: Properness of the straight-line homotopy on the cylinder [0,1] × S
subproblems.statement:
Let m, m′ ∈ ℕ, let F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} be continuous, let S ⊆ ℝ^m be closed and let s ∈ ℝ. Assume that dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s for every x ∈ S, and that F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ S is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}.

Notation:
- ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p).
- t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)) for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}.
- G(y) := F₀(tl y) + t(y)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)), the straight-line homotopy, written exactly as in dph_sh_affine_estimate.
- cyl(S) := {y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ S}.

Then G⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(S) is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}. No sign condition on s is assumed or needed.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the supplied proof of dph_sh_affine_estimate (closedness of the cylinder and properness of G; Simon Ch. 6, 2.25/2.27), stated for an arbitrary closed set S in place of spt X. Notation as in the statement. Put e := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ and e′ := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ.

1. (Continuity and the shape of the cylinder.) t = tL := (ContinuousLinearMap.proj 0) ∘L e and tl = tlL := e′.symm ∘L (ContinuousLinearMap.pi (j ↦ ContinuousLinearMap.proj j.succ)) ∘L e are continuous linear maps. Both identities hold definitionally, because Fin.tail q = (j ↦ q j.succ). Therefore:
   - G = F₀∘tlL + tL·(F₁∘tlL − F₀∘tlL) is continuous, being built from compositions, differences, scalar products and sums of continuous maps;
   - cyl(S) = tL⁻¹([0,1]) ∩ tlL⁻¹(S).

2. (The set is closed.) Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}. K is closed, because compact subsets of the Hausdorff space ℝ^{m′} are closed (IsCompact.isClosed). So G⁻¹(K) is closed. Since [0,1] and S are closed and tL, tlL are continuous, cyl(S) is closed. Hence C := G⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(S) is closed.

3. (A compact superset.)
   - K_s := cthickening s K is compact, because ℝ^{m′} is a proper metric space (IsCompact.cthickening; no sign condition on s is needed).
   - By hypothesis P := F₀⁻¹(K_s) ∩ S is compact, so [0,1] × P is compact (isCompact_Icc.prod).
   - The map Φ : ℝ × ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1}, Φ(τ, x) := cons(τ, x) = e.symm (Fin.cons τ (e′ x)), is continuous. It is the continuous linear map (τ, x) ↦ Fin.cons τ (e′ x) (ContinuousLinearMap.finCons of fst and e′ ∘L snd) followed by the continuous e.symm.
   - Therefore Q := Φ([0,1] × P) is compact (IsCompact.image).

4. (C ⊆ Q.) Let y ∈ C and put τ := t(y) and x := tl(y). Then G(y) ∈ K, τ ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ S.
   (a) Φ(τ, x) = y. Indeed e′ x = e′ (e′.symm (Fin.tail (e y))) = Fin.tail (e y) and τ = (e y) 0. So Fin.cons τ (e′ x) = Fin.cons ((e y) 0) (Fin.tail (e y)) = e y (Fin.cons_self_tail), and e.symm (e y) = y.
   (b) F₀(x) ∈ K_s. By definition G(y) = F₀(x) + τ·(F₁(x) − F₀(x)), so F₀(x) − G(y) = −(τ·(F₁(x) − F₀(x))). Hence dist(F₀(x), G(y)) = ‖τ·(F₁(x) − F₀(x))‖ = |τ|·‖F₁(x) − F₀(x)‖ = τ·dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)), using τ ≥ 0 and dist_eq_norm. Since τ ≤ 1 and dist ≥ 0, this is ≤ 1·dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s, by the hypothesis at x ∈ S. As G(y) ∈ K, Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le gives F₀(x) ∈ cthickening s K = K_s.
   Hence x ∈ P, so (τ, x) ∈ [0,1] × P and y = Φ(τ, x) ∈ Q.

5. (Conclusion.) By steps 2–4, C is a closed subset of the compact set Q, so C is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). Since K was an arbitrary compact set, G⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(S) is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}. ∎
proof_key_steps: t and tl are continuous linear, so G is continuous and cyl(S) = t⁻¹[0,1] ∩ tl⁻¹(S) is closed; hence G⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(S) is closed for compact (hence closed) K.
Q := cons([0,1] × (F₀⁻¹(cthickening s K) ∩ S)) is compact: the cthickening of a compact set is compact, the properness hypothesis applies, and (τ,x) ↦ cons(τ,x) is continuous.
For y ∈ G⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(S): y = cons(t y, tl y) by Fin.cons_self_tail, and dist(F₀(tl y), G y) = t(y)·dist(F₁(tl y), F₀(tl y)) ≤ s, so F₀(tl y) ∈ cthickening s K and y ∈ Q.
A closed subset of a compact set is compact.
